transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My mind just won’t slow down—ideas are racing all the time and I can’t keep my thoughts straight anymore. It's just gotten to the point where it's really hard to get through my day because everything is so jumbled up.

Before this episode, have you ever had a period of at least a few days or longer when you felt unusually depressed, down, or lost interest in things? Or is this the first major mood episode you’ve had?

I'm not really sure, but I don't think I've ever had periods of feeling deeply depressed before this whole situation started about a year and a half ago. This is really the first time my mood and mind have been so out of whack.

Have you ever had hallucinations or strong unusual beliefs continue for at least 2 weeks when your mood was otherwise normal—not especially high, irritable, or depressed? Or do those symptoms only happen when your mood is clearly elevated or agitated?

Yes, that actually happened this past winter when my mood and energy had dropped back to a normal, "so-so" level for a while. Even though I felt pretty even-keeled, I was still convinced people at work were trying to sabotage me and I kept hearing my name whispered when I was alone.

When those suspicious thoughts and whispered voices continued, did they last for at least 2 weeks while your mood stayed basically normal the whole time? Or were there still any periods of feeling unusually high, irritable, or depressed during those two weeks?

Yes, it definitely lasted for at least two or three weeks, and my mood stayed completely flat and "so-so" the whole time. I wasn't feeling high, irritable, or down at all, but the whispers and the feeling that people were sabotaging me just kept going.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) that persisted for at least 2–3 weeks during a period of euthymic/normal mood, which is the key distinguishing feature of schizoaffective disorder, manic type. There is also evidence of a mood episode with racing thoughts and disturbed thinking, and the overall course has lasted about 1.5 years. The available differential list contains only F25.0, which best fits the interview data.
